headline: Nor’easter’s worst wind passes, but rain and flooding concerns remain
dek: The National Weather Service says the strongest winds have eased across southern New England, while rain, minor coastal flooding and localized street flooding remain possible into Monday.
body: The worst of the nor’easter’s wind has moved through southern New England, but the National Weather Service Boston/Norton office says unsettled weather will continue. Its Sunday morning discussion says windswept rain, minor coastal flooding and beach erosion remain possible, along with localized urban and street flooding, through Monday.

The office canceled High Wind Warnings and Wind Advisories for eastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island as conditions eased. A Flood Watch remains in effect for parts of the region, and forecasters continue to warn that repeated downpours could overwhelm urban drainage and other low-lying areas.

The Boston-area forecast calls for more showers Sunday and Monday, with some periods of heavy rain. Northeast winds remain strong enough to make travel difficult in exposed locations, even though the most damaging gusts are no longer expected to dominate the event.

Residents should monitor the latest local alerts, avoid driving through water covering a roadway and use caution near the coast. The exact combination of rain, wind and coastal impacts will vary by community as the low gradually weakens.
author: NorthEast News Desk
